thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired: High 5xx error rate detected on service `inference-gateway-eu-west1`

pagerduty: PD Alert: Alert #A-98321 auto-triggered (high-5xx-rate). Escalation policy: inference-oncall.

Maria: acking — I'm on it, joining in 30s. Oncall window: Maria -> Alex in 50m.

Alex: oncall handoff noted. Maria if you need a fast follow ping me.

Jamie: quick metrics from dashboards — 1m error-rate jumped from 0.3% -> 16.8% at 12:14UTC. 502s are the majority. Throughput roughly constant.

Kai: logs show a bunch of `upstream reset` and `connection refused` from the sidecar pool to backend inference pods:```
[12:14:22] inference-gateway -> backend-pool-7: connection reset by peer
[12:14:23] 502 GET /v1/generate 45ms
[12:14:24] backend-pool-9: failed to allocate kv-cache
```

Elena: checking deploys — git history: last deploy to eu-west1 was 3h ago, no canary active. No cron jobs.

Maria: rolling quick health checks. Running: `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep eu-west1` and `curl -sSf http://inference-gateway.eu-west1/health`

Alex: also checking infra: LB target health in cloud console looks flapping for 3 of 12 ingress nodes. Might be transient network to the infra-managed KV cache.

incident-bot: Incident notes: alerts linked to PD incident A-98321. Runbook: `inference-502-spike` suggested actions: scale backend, drain failing nodes, reroute traffic to fallback model.

Maria: scaling backend pool +20% now via autoscaler override (temp). Command: `redwoodctl scale backend eu-west1 --replicas 1200` (approx).

Jamie: adding a temporary fallback routing rule to send non-critical requests to model-variant `small-v2` to reduce backend pressure.

Kai: I see repeated `kv-cache` allocation timeouts in kube events. Could be OOM or kernel tweaks. Looking at node memory.

Elena: support-bot, can you surface whether any customers have open errors? Run the customer-impact query.

support-bot: Notifying CS team. Support dashboard shows ~18% of requests failing for 3 enterprise customers (tenant ids: 2941, 4102, 7183). Severity: medium-high. Preparing customer ping draft.

Maria: immediate mitigation checklist: 1) scale backend pool (done), 2) add fallback routing (done), 3) drain flaky nodes (in progress), 4) disable keepalive proxy pooling on ingress (tentative), 5) open follow-up on kv-cache root cause.

Alex: I'm going to cordon+drain node eu-node-7 that shows repeated connection resets. Will be quick.

Kai: node eu-node-7 shows `oom_kill` on kv-cache process at 12:12UTC. Suspect memory pressure after cache eviction thrash. Draining is fine.

incident-bot: action log: Maria scaled pool; Jamie updated routing; Alex draining eu-node-7; Kai investigating kv-cache.

Maria: after scaling and routing change, error rate dropping to 6.2% at 12:25UTC. Still above baseline but improving. :thumbsup:

Jamie: performing health checks on backend pods — 3 pods restarted in last 7m, others healthy. No new deploys.

Elena: Support drafted customer note: "We saw elevated error rates affecting some requests in eu-west region between 12:14-12:28 UTC. We have mitigations in place and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a post-incident report." Approving send?

Maria: send to CS now. Also adding reminder to include mitigation steps and ETA for RCA.

pagerduty: PD: A-98321 status changed to "acknowledged" by Maria.

Kai: dug into kv-cache agent — there is a regression in the eviction loop introduced in version 1.12.4 that increases memory churn under certain sequence lengths. eu cluster was running 1.12.4. US clusters are on 1.12.3 and unaffected.

Alex: that explains it. Plan: roll back kv-cache agent to 1.12.3 on eu-west1 as hotfix. Maria can you approve?

Maria: approve rollback. Jamie coordinate with infra for a staged rollback. Prefer canary 10% -> 50% -> full.

Jamie: initiating rolling rollback. Command: `k8s-deploy --namespace infra kv-cache-agent:1.12.3 --strategy rolling --max-unavailable 1`

incident-bot: automated runbook step executed: rollback started at 12:32UTC.

Maria: after first batch of rollbacks, error rate down to 1.1% at 12:40UTC. Customer errors falling.

support-bot: CS notified all impacted customers with initial message and monitoring link. No escalations yet.

Kai: monitoring heap and alloc rates — back to baseline. Looks like rollback resolved the memory churn.

Alex: I'm going to re-enable normal autoscaling and remove temporary routing by end of next 10m if stable.

Maria: agree. Leaving a 30m watch. If stable, we'll close PD incident and open postmortem ticket.

Jamie: quick note: created task PM-7421 to track root cause and preventative measures (tests for eviction-edge-cases, version gating).

Elena: adding post-incident notify to #product and #security since kv-cache touches sensitive configs.

incident-bot: PD Incident A-98321 auto-resolve will trigger when no alerts in 30m. Current status: acknowledged -> mitigated.

Alex: final check — last 10m error-rate 0.4% which is within baseline. Rolling back the temporary routing now.

Maria: closing timeline: 12:14UTC alert, 12:32UTC rollback trigger, 12:40UTC errors near baseline. Postmortem + follow-ups assigned.

Jamie: thumbs for team coordination. :partyparrot: Good runbook execution.

Elena: marking this as a candidate for runbook update to include kv-cache version checks on deploys.

support-bot: CS will send a follow-up summary to impacted customers tomorrow with RCA link.

pagerduty: PD: A-98321 status changed to "resolved" by Maria at 12:50UTC.

Maria: if anyone finds lingering logs or anomalies, ping this thread. Otherwise I'll file the postmortem draft later today.

Alex: noted. Thanks all — nice quick work. :heart:

incident-bot: Thread closed for monitoring. Remember to attach logs + timeline to the PM ticket.
